concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 2 – Core utility library (single‑module group) – T004
concerns.text: Task T004 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it writes/updates shared modules (`code/utils/`) that are later read and modified by subsequent tasks (e.g., T010, T011, T013, T014). Because these scripts share mutable state (files in `code/` and `data/processed/`), they are not safe to run in parallel; the `[P]` tag is therefore inaccurate.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 5 – Power analysis & reference‑power computation (US‑3) – T010
concerns.text: Task T010 is also marked `[P]` yet it reads from `statistical_params.jsonl` and writes `power_audit_results.jsonl` and `power_summary.json`. These artifacts are consumed by T011 and later tasks, so concurrent execution would cause race conditions. The `[P]` tag should be removed or the task re‑engineered to be truly side‑effect‑free.

Task T011 is marked `[P]` but it depends on the outputs of T010 (`power_audit_results.jsonl`) and T008 (`extraction_audit.json`). Running it in parallel with its producers would break the data‑flow. The parallel‑safe annotation is incorrect.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 7 – Reproducible execution & user‑facing documentation – T012
concerns.text: Task T012 is tagged `[P]` yet it orchestrates the sequential execution of all previous pipeline scripts. Its purpose is inherently sequential, so the `[P]` tag misrepresents its execution model.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 8 – Performance limits, provenance, and checksum manifest – T013
concerns.text: Task T013 adds runtime‑ and memory‑limit checks to every pipeline script, modifying many existing scripts. Because it mutates the same code files that other tasks rely on, it cannot be safely run in parallel with those tasks; the `[P]` tag is therefore invalid.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 8 – Performance limits, provenance, and checksum manifest – T014
concerns.text: Task T014 appends entries to `data/processed/checksum_manifest.json` after each pipeline stage. Since earlier tasks (e.g., T007, T008, T010) also write checksum information to `data/metadata.json`, having two separate manifest files creates a potential inconsistency and violates the Single Source of Truth principle. The task should target the canonical `data/metadata.json` instead of a separate manifest.

User‑story blocks are required to be independently shippable units. US‑2 (T008) and US‑3 (T010) both depend on the outputs of the preceding user stories (US‑1 produces `filtered_datasets.json`; US‑2 produces `statistical_params.jsonl`). This violates the “independently‑shippable” rule; each story should either include its upstream producers or be re‑structured so it can be executed end‑to‑end without external prerequisites.
